oneLiner: The largest installed base in consumer tech (2.5B+ active devices), now run by John Ternus, monetised through a premium iPhone cycle and a high-margin Services layer. The market is betting that FY2026's double-digit growth is a new run-rate driven by the foldable and Siri AI, not a one-off upgrade wave that fades as memory costs squeeze margins.

verdict.summary: FY2026 was Apple's best growth year since FY2021 and the September quarter beat, but the December-quarter guide shows the next leg is harder: growth slows to 7-10% on constrained supply, gross margin steps down on memory costs, and Services decelerates. The price already capitalises the supercycle at a mid-30s multiple, so our probability-weighted value sits below the current quote: the bull case needs both mid-teens revenue growth and a held multiple, while the bear case only needs the multiple to drift toward its long-run mid-20s. We would turn more positive if the March-quarter guide holds high-single-digit growth with gross margin back above 46.5%, or on a material pullback with the cycle intact.
wtb: FY2027 revenue grows ~10% to about $525B or more, i.e. supply catches up with iPhone 18 Pro and Duo demand by the March 2027 quarter rather than demand fading.
Gross margin bottoms in the 45-46% guided range in the December 2026 quarter and recovers toward 47% by mid-2027 as price increases offset memory costs.
Services grows at least 8% a year through FY2027 even if the D.C. Circuit restricts Google's default-search payments.
The market keeps paying ~30x+ trailing EPS at end-2027, which requires the reverse-DCF bar (~14% a year FCF growth for a decade) to look reachable rather than a FY2026 one-off.

thesis: The upgrade cycle is real. FY2026 revenue grew 15% after three years averaging under 2%, with iPhone up 21% for the year; demand is outrunning supply, not the reverse.

Pricing power offsets cost inflation. Apple raised iPhone 17 prices by $100 at the iPhone 18 Pro launch and lifted some MacBook prices, and the $1,999 iPhone Duo opens a new tier (Bloomberg Intelligence: $28-32B of FY2027 sales).
China turned from a drag into a driver. Greater China grew 28% in FY2026 and 21% in the September quarter, reversing the multi-year share loss to Huawei.
Per-share compounding. The diluted share count fell 1.6% YoY in FQ4 and $100B of buyback authority (April 2026) keeps shrinking it, so EPS grows faster than profit.
Earnings are cash. FY2026 operating cash flow of $145.1B exceeded net income, and capex stays near 2% of revenue while megacap peers pour cash into AI data centers.

latestQuarter.label: Q4 FY2026 (ended Sep 26, 2026; reported Nov 2, 2026)
points: Revenue $114.5B, +12% YoY, a September-quarter record, vs ~$113.4B LSEG consensus; FY2026 revenue $478.8B, +15%.
Diluted EPS $2.10, +14% (vs ~$1.99 consensus), including $0.05 from tariff refunds; FY2026 EPS $8.98 vs $7.46.
Gross margin 47.9% including ~1pt from tariff refunds; operating income $35.6B, +10%.
Guide: December quarter revenue +7-10% YoY, gross margin 45-46%, Services +8-9%; shares fell ~2-4% during the call.

latestProse: Q4 FY2026 (ended Sep 26; reported Nov 2), John Ternus' first call as CEO. Revenue $114.5B (+12%) beat consensus; iPhone grew 17% and Mac 24%, while iPad and Wearables shrank. Greater China rose to $17.5B from $14.5B a year earlier. Net income was $30.7B and diluted EPS $2.10 (+14%) on 14.63B diluted shares. Tariff refunds flattered the print by ~1pt of gross margin and $0.05 of EPS, and CFO Kevan Parekh said Apple has now received the vast majority of the refunds owed, so that support ends. Apple returned ~$28B to shareholders in the quarter and kept the dividend at $0.27. Purchase commitments rose ~$33B in the quarter; COO Sabih Khan would not confirm a long-term memory supply deal.
guidanceProse: December-quarter guide: revenue +7-10% YoY (about $153.8-158.1B against $143.8B a year ago), which would still be Apple's largest quarter ever but brackets a ~$153.4B consensus only at the low end. Gross margin 45-46%, down from 47.9%: Parekh blamed memory costs, expected to keep rising into 2027, and the cost of ramping Siri AI; ex-refunds the step-down is 1-2pts. Services +8-9% vs ~10.7% expected, citing third-party licensing and FX. Ternus said supply is 'constrained as of today' with no date for balance, and a very small share of iPhone Duo units have been returned for display issues and are being replaced.
segments: iPhone ~53% of FY2026 revenue ($254.1B, +21%): iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and the $1,999 iPhone Duo foldable (shipping since Oct 23) lead the cycle.
Services ~26% ($123.3B, +13%): App Store, iCloud, advertising, licensing (incl. Google default-search payments); ~76% gross margin in FQ4.
Mac ~8% ($37.9B, +13%); Wearables, Home and Accessories ~7% ($35.6B, flat); iPad ~6% ($27.9B, flat).
Geography FY2026: Americas $198.1B, Europe $127.6B, Greater China $82.4B, Rest of Asia Pacific $39.9B, Japan $30.9B.
competitive: Google is both supplier (Gemini underpins Siri AI) and rival (Pixel, Android); Apple rents the frontier-model layer rather than owning it.
Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold now faces the iPhone Duo at the top of the foldable market.
Huawei remains the main China rival, but Apple regained share in FY2026.
Memory makers and Nvidia-led AI demand compete with Apple for DRAM/NAND and TSMC leading-node capacity, which is why supply and cost, not demand, set the near-term guide.
moat: An installed base above 2.5 billion active devices with deep ecosystem lock-in (App Store, iCloud, iMessage, silicon-software integration) drives industry-best hardware margins and a recurring Services stream. Custom silicon and scale purchasing give first claim on leading-edge capacity, though AI demand now contests that claim.
risks: The price needs the cycle to persist. The reverse DCF needs ~14% a year FCF growth for a decade against ~2% a year revenue growth over FY2023-FY2025; FY2026's 15% has to be the start of a trend, and the December guide already slows to 7-10%.
Memory costs compress margins. Gross margin is guided down to 45-46% with memory costs rising into 2027 and tariff refunds ending; each point of gross margin is roughly $5B of annual pre-tax profit.
Services is decelerating into legal risk. Growth is guided to 8-9%, and DOJ is asking the D.C. Circuit to ban Google's default-search payments, a high-margin licensing stream.
Supply and quality execution. Supply has no stated balance date and some Duo units have been returned for display issues; a holiday shortfall defers revenue and risks losing buyers.
Legal overhangs. A Sept 25, 2026 jury found Apple owes over $5.7B to Taction over Taptic Engine patents; Apple is appealing (status since unverified).
catalysts: Mid-Nov 2026 (reported, unverified): smart-home hub shipping after the Oct 13 'Welcome Home' launch - first new Siri AI device category.
~Late Jan 2027 (date not yet confirmed): Q1 FY2027 report - December quarter vs the +7-10% guide, gross margin vs 45-46%, March-quarter guide (debates 1 and 2).
Pending: D.C. Circuit ruling on Google default-search payments (debate 3); Apple's appeal of the Taction verdict.
~Late Apr/early May 2027: Q2 FY2027 report and the annual buyback authorization (debates 1 and 3).
June 2027: WWDC - next Siri AI step and whether Apple deepens or loosens its Gemini dependence (debate 3).

bear.why: Supply stays tight into mid-2027 and the cycle fades after the holiday quarter; revenue grows ~4%, memory costs hold gross margin near 45% and net margin falls to 25%. Services slows toward mid-single digits if the Google payments are curtailed. With growth back to the FY2023-25 pace, the multiple reverts toward Apple's long-run mid-20s.

base.why: Supply catches up by the March quarter, the Duo adds a new tier and revenue grows ~10%; price increases offset most memory inflation, so net margin eases only to ~26.5% from FY2026's 27.6% (which included refunds). The market pays a premium trailing multiple for a durable cycle plus buybacks, but below today's level as growth normalises.

bull.why: Siri AI and the Duo extend the cycle across the installed base: revenue grows ~16% for a second year, memory costs ease in 2H FY2027 and net margin holds ~27.5%. Two years of mid-teens growth make the reverse-DCF bar look reachable, so the mid-30s multiple holds.

scenarioModel.note: EPS = revenue x net margin / ~14.4B diluted shares (14.63B in FQ4 FY26, shrinking ~1.6% a year). Bear $500B x 25.0% = $125.0B / 14.4B = $8.68; base $525B x 26.5% = $139.1B / 14.4B = $9.66; bull $555B x 27.5% = $152.6B / 14.4B = $10.60. FY2026 was $478.8B revenue, $132.2B net income (27.6%), $8.98 EPS. Multiples are applied to FY2027 EPS at end-2027 (a trailing multiple by then). Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus; pre-print FY2027 consensus EPS was ~$9.5 (MarketBeat/aggregators, July 2026, unverified post-print).

debates.q: Is FY2026's 15% growth a new run-rate or a one-off upgrade wave?
debates.bull: Demand is supply-limited, not fading: the guide is capped by component supply, the Duo opens a new price tier, Greater China is growing again and Siri AI gives the 2.5B-device base a reason to upgrade.
debates.bear: Revenue grew under 2% a year from FY2023 to FY2025; the December guide already halves the growth rate, and upgrade waves (FY2021) have historically been followed by flat years.
debates.view: This sets the multiple (24x vs 36x). The base case assumes ~10% growth, which is above the December guide's midpoint; we need the March quarter to confirm before paying up.

signpost.threshold: bullish if +8% or more; bearish if below +5%

debates.q: Can pricing offset memory inflation, or is the gross margin peak behind us?
debates.bull: Apple has already raised iPhone 17 and some Mac prices, holds inventory bought at lower memory prices, and Services (76% gross margin) is a growing share of the mix.
debates.bear: The 45-46% guide is a 1-2pt step-down even ex-refunds, Parekh expects memory costs to keep rising into 2027, and the Siri AI ramp adds cost Apple cannot charge for directly.
debates.view: A margin dip in a constrained holiday quarter is tolerable; a second quarter below 45% would move us toward the bear case's 25% net margin.

signpost.metric: Reported FQ1 gross margin and FQ2 gross margin guide
signpost.threshold: below 45% = bearish; guide back above 46.5% = bullish

debates.q: Does Services keep compounding at 8%+ through the Google remedy?
debates.bull: A 2.5B-device base, price increases and new Siri AI features keep attach rising; even a payments ban could be replaced by a revenue-share search or AI deal.
debates.bear: Services growth slowed from 13% in FY2026 to an 8-9% guide, and the Google default payments are almost pure profit; a ban hits EPS directly.
debates.view: Services is the multiple's floor. Sub-8% growth plus an adverse ruling would take the base-case multiple toward the mid-20s.

signpost.metric: Services revenue growth YoY; D.C. Circuit ruling on default-search payments
signpost.threshold: below 8% for two quarters, or a payments ban upheld
signpost.when: Q1-Q2 FY2027 reports (Jan-May 2027); ruling date unknown

valPresets.note: Apple converts earnings to cash with little capex, so FCF is the honest basis. The base preset (8%, fading) sits well below the ~14% a year the reverse DCF says is priced in - that gap is the valuation argument in one number.
